title: Growth Trends in Key Regions
text:
Regional GDP Growth Trends (2000–2023)
This page explores GDP growth trends in three key regions—East Asia & Pacific, Sub-Saharan Africa, and Latin America & Caribbean—from 2000 to 2023, using data from the World Bank’s World Development Indicators. By focusing on these regions, we uncover distinct patterns of economic performance, from rapid growth to periods of volatility, shaped by global events like the 2008 financial crisis. The visualizations below highlight both average growth trends and the variability within each region, offering insights into their economic stability.
Average GDP Growth Over Time
The line plot below shows the average annual GDP growth for each region, revealing how growth trajectories differ across East Asia & Pacific, Sub-Saharan Africa, and Latin America & Caribbean.









East Asia & Pacific consistently shows higher and more stable growth, while Sub-Saharan Africa and Latin America & Caribbean exhibit greater fluctuations, particularly around 2008–2009.
Variability in GDP Growth
The box plot below illustrates the distribution of GDP growth within each region, highlighting differences in economic stability across countries.









The box plot reveals that Sub-Saharan Africa has the widest range of GDP growth, indicating significant variability across countries, while East Asia & Pacific shows a tighter distribution, suggesting greater economic consistency. These patterns align with the model results, which highlight the role of investment and trade in driving stable growth.

title: About
text:
I’m Faran Abbas, a graduate student specializing in World Economy. My academic interests include international trade, fiscal policy, and economic development in emerging markets. You can explore my work and projects on GitHub, or reach me via email at faranabbas@hotmail.com.
This project analyzes how fiscal policy and international trade have influenced GDP growth across countries from 2000 to 2023. It combines data visualization, policy analysis, and economic indicators using data sourced from the World Bank. The full project repository is available here.
This project was developed as part of Kane’s Data Science Bootcamp, which emphasizes reproducible research and open-source tools using R and Quarto.

title: Data Sources
text:
Data Sources
The data for this project was sourced from the World Bank’s World Development Indicators (WDI) database, accessed via the WDI R package, covering the period from 2000 to 2023. Key variables include GDP growth (annual percentage change), income per capita (current US dollars), trade openness (exports as a percentage of GDP), investment (gross capital formation as a percentage of GDP), inflation (consumer price index), and unemployment (percentage of the labor force). The raw data was cleaned by removing observations with missing values to ensure robust analysis. No specific countries or years were excluded beyond those with incomplete data, resulting in a balanced panel dataset suitable for fixed-effects modeling.

title: Data Sources
text:
Preceptor Table







Component
Details




Population
All economies in the WDI database (2000–2024), ~217 economies, excluding aggregates.


Causal Question
How do trade openness, fiscal balance, health expenditure, education, infrastructure, and private sector credit influence GDP and GNI per capita?


Treatment
Trade openness (NE.TRD.GNFS.ZS), fiscal balance (GC.REV.XGRT.GD.ZS).


Covariates
Health expenditure (SH.XPD.TOTL.ZS), primary enrollment (SE.PRM.ENRR), electric power consumption (EG.USE.ELEC.KH.PC), domestic credit (FS.AST.PRVT.GD.ZS), year, region, income level.


Outcome
Primary: Log GDP (NY.GDP.MKTP.CD). Alternative: Log GNI per capita (NY.GNP.PCAP.CD).


Data Source
WDI via WDI R package: NY.GDP.MKTP.CD, NY.GNP.PCAP.CD, NE.TRD.GNFS.ZS, GC.REV.XGRT.GD.ZS, SH.XPD.TOTL.ZS, SE.PRM.ENRR, EG.USE.ELEC.KH.PC, FS.AST.PRVT.GD.ZS.


Time Frame
2000–2024, annual data.


Units
Country-year observations.


Potential Outcomes
Expected log GDP and log GNI per capita under varying treatments and covariates.


Missing Data
Excluded observations with missing values for key variables. No imputation.


Analysis Plan
Visualizations, multiple linear regression, regional comparisons.

title: Data Sources
text:
Data Sources
Data was sourced from the World Bank’s WDI using the WDI R package, covering over 200 economies (2000–2024). Indicators: - GDP (NY.GDP.MKTP.CD): Nominal GDP in current US\(.
- **GNI per Capita (NY.GNP.PCAP.CD)**: GNI per capita in current US\). - Trade Openness (NE.TRD.GNFS.ZS): Trade as % of GDP. - Fiscal Balance (GC.REV.XGRT.GD.ZS): Government revenue as % of GDP. - Health Expenditure (SH.XPD.TOTL.ZS): Total health expenditure as % of GDP. - Primary Enrollment (SE.PRM.ENRR): Gross enrollment ratio (%). - Electric Power Consumption (EG.USE.ELEC.KH.PC): Power consumption per capita (kWh). - Domestic Credit (FS.AST.PRVT.GD.ZS): Credit to private sector as % of GDP.

title: Data Sources
text:
Cleaning Process

Retrieved data for all economies without country-specific filters.
Excluded regional aggregates (income != "Aggregates").
Removed rows with missing values for key variables to ensure data integrity.
Applied log transformation (log(gdp + 1), log(gni_per_capita + 1)) to handle scale differences.
No imputation was performed to maintain accuracy.
